Findings written to `findings.md`. Summary of the defects introduced by the diff:

**`src/sync.py`**
- `:14` — pagination uses floor division (`total_count // PAGE_SIZE`), so the last partial page is never fetched (e.g. 250 users → only 200 fetched; under 100 → none).
- `:24` — `seen=[]` mutable default persists across calls, so IDs from earlier syncs are skipped forever.
- `:31` — IDs are appended to `seen` before the UPDATE runs, so failed users are marked seen and never retried.
- `:35` — parameterized SQL replaced with an f-string: SQL injection risk, and any email containing `'` (e.g. `o'brien@x.com`) breaks the statement.
- `:39` — `except Exception: pass` replaces the logging, silently hiding all sync failures.

**`src/report.py`**
- `:7` — early `return 0` on empty users skips `f.close()`, leaking the file handle.
- `:11` — `user["email"].lower().split("@")[1]` crashes on `None` emails (the schema notes in `src/db.py` explicitly warn email is nullable) and on addresses without `@`; the old code handled `None` via `or "unverified"`.
